# dsh-jupyterlab
**A JupyterLab-style notebook for DeepSeek Harness.** A real, persistent `ipykernel` the agent can r
ead, edit and run — with a front end that behaves like JupyterLab: code on the left, figures on the
right, Jupyter keyboard shortcuts, and Markdown cells.

> **This is a modified fork of `@beihaizb/dsh-notebook` by beihzb (MIT).**
> The kernel sidecar, the
`nb_*` agent tools, `.ipynb` save/load and the cell UI are upstream work. This package keeps all of
it and adds the features below, as a single self-contained plugin (the upstream sources are vendore
d, so `dsh plugin add` installs everything).
## What this fork adds
1. **Split view (code | output).** Every code cell renders as two columns: the editor on the left, i
ts outputs — figures, stdout, DataFrames, tracebacks — on the right. A draggable divider resizes the
columns and the ratio is remembered. The toolbar button `⇔ Split` / `⇕ Inline` returns to the class

ic stacked layout.
2. **Outputs stay in sight.** The output pane is bottom-aligned and sticks to the
viewport while you scroll a long cell, so a figure you just rendered is already on screen instead o

f being stranded at the top of the cell.
3. **Jupyter keyboard shortcuts.** Press `Esc` to leave edi
ting (command mode), then `a` / `b` insert a cell above / below, `dd` deletes, `Enter` edits, `↑` `↓
` (or `k` `j`) move, `m` / `y` switch the cell to Markdown / Code, and `Ctrl+Enter` / `Shift+Enter`
/ `Alt+Enter` run. While editing, `Tab` accepts the completion popup (and still indents when none is

open). `?` opens the shortcut list.
4. **Cell type and one-click delete.** A `✂` scissors in the gu
tter deletes the cell, and a `py` / `md` chip shows and switches the cell type. Markdown cells rende

r `##` headings, are edited by double-click, and can be folded like code cells.
5. **`+ MD` in the t

oolbar** inserts a Markdown cell (the existing `+ Cell` now selects and focuses what it inserts).
6.
**Left file bar (JupyterLab-style).** The saved `.ipynb` files in the working directory are listed

down the left side; click one to open it. The toolbar `🗂 Files` button shows/hides the bar.
7. **Rig
ht figure viewer.** Click any output figure — or any image path printed in the output, such as `Save
d: ...\fig.tif` — and it opens in a resizable panel on the right (fit / actual size / fullscreen / c
lose) instead of a modal that covers the notebook. `.tif` / `.tiff` frames are converted to PNG with
the kernel's Pillow and cached, so saved TIFFs preview too.
Everything else — persistent kernel, agent tools, `.ipynb` round-trip, kernel picker, tqdm progress
bars, clickable tracebacks, long-output folding, hybrid-CPU hint, EN/中文 UI — is upstream and unchang
s, clickable tracebacks, long-output folding, hybrid-CPU hint, EN/中文 UI — is upstream and unchanged.

From the GitHub repository (this is what the plugin market uses):

Or from the prebuilt tarball attached to the latest GitHub Release (no build step):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart DeepSeek Harness. A **Notebook** tab appears in the session.
The package ships its compiled `lib/` and the Python driver, so there is nothing to build at install
time (no `prepare` / install scripts — pnpm has no build to approve).
> **Don't install this next to `@beihaizb/dsh-notebook`.** Both register the same `nb_*` tools; this

fork is a superset, so remove the original first:
>

The Python environment you pick as kernel needs `ipykernel`, `jupyter_client` and `nbformat`.

`nb_add_cell` also accepts `before` (insert above a given cell) in this fork.
## Compatibility
Developed and tested against DSH `0.2.1-rc.5` on Windows with a conda `ipykernel`.
